reasoning: Recent Maine Senate polling in the last 45 days shows a very close race, with multiple polls giving Democrat Troy Jackson a narrow edge over Republican Susan Collins and one August poll putting Jackson up by 4 points. Independent aggregate/forecast pages also show only a small Republican advantage or near-tie, but those are better treated as context rather than direct current-race polls. Maine’s statewide Cook PVI is D+6.

sources.name: Portland Press Herald / University of New Hampshire Survey Center poll
sources.details: University of New Hampshire poll of likely general election voters found Troy Jackson leading Susan Collins 49% to 46% in a hypothetical Senate matchup.

sources.name: Spectrum Local News / University of New Hampshire Pine Tree State Poll
sources.details: Spectrum reported the same UNH poll as a statistical tie, with Jackson ahead 49% to 46% and a margin of error near 3%.

sources.name: Bangor Daily News / Hart Research poll
sources.details: Hart Research poll found Jackson leading Collins 49% to 45%, a 4-point Democratic edge.

sources.name: PollsMax Maine Senate polling average
sources.details: PollsMax aggregate showed a statewide Senate polling average of 46.8% for the Democrat and 47.3% for the Republican, a 0.5-point Republican edge.
